about_text:
MapBarber {version}
Trim stray voxels, points and pixels, and fill the bald spots in robot maps.
controls_general:
Open maps with Ctrl+O or drop files onto the window. Each file opens in its own tab:

· .bt / .ot / voxel .npz → voxel map editor
· .pcd / .ply / .xyz / .csv / .npy → point cloud editor
· map .yaml / .pgm / .png → 2D occupancy grid editor

Ctrl+Tab / Ctrl+Shift+Tab: next / previous tab   ·   Ctrl+W: close tab
controls_voxel:
Left drag: rotate   ·   Middle drag or Space + drag: pan   ·   Wheel or Ctrl+= / Ctrl+−: zoom
1 front · 3 side · 7 top · 0 / Home: isometric

Tools:  H navigate   V select   E erase   B add   I measure
[ / ]: smaller / larger brush
Select: click selects the brush cube   ·   right click: deselect   ·   Ctrl + drag: paint with the brush while the view stays still
Erase: click removes the brush cube
Add: click a voxel face to grow one layer; click empty space to place voxels on the work plane
Measure: click two points; hold Shift to lock to an axis

Shift + drag: rectangle select   ·   Shift + right drag: rectangle deselect
Delete: erase selection   ·   Backspace: undo last selection step   ·   Esc / Ctrl+D: deselect
Ctrl+A: select all visible   ·   Ctrl+Shift+I: invert selection
Box: drag the coloured arrows to move it along x / y / z, the dots to resize it
Slice: cut the space with a plane, edit one side, then Restore view
Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Shift+Z (Ctrl+Y): undo / redo   ·   Ctrl+S: save

Labelling mode (Ctrl+L):  B label brush   ·   Ctrl+1 … Ctrl+9: label the selection with the n-th class   ·   Enter: active class   ·   Ctrl+0: clear   ·   P: protect labelled voxels
Smart pick W finds a connected object, a flat or a smooth surface   ·   Delete clears labels (voxels stay)   ·   Ctrl + right drag: take back with the brush
controls_cloud:
Left drag: rotate   ·   Middle drag or Space + drag: pan   ·   Wheel or Ctrl+= / Ctrl+−: zoom
1 front · 3 side · 7 top · 0 / Home: isometric

Tools:  H navigate   V select   E erase   I measure
[ / ]: smaller / larger brush radius
Select / Erase: click a point to affect every point inside the brush sphere   ·   right click: deselect   ·   Ctrl + drag: paint with the brush while the view stays still
Measure: click two points; hold Shift to lock to an axis
Noise filters only select; press Delete to remove what they found.

Shift + drag: rectangle select   ·   Shift + right drag: rectangle deselect
Delete: erase selection   ·   Backspace: undo last selection step   ·   Esc / Ctrl+D: deselect
Ctrl+A: select all visible   ·   Ctrl+Shift+I: invert selection
Box: drag the coloured arrows to move it along x / y / z, the dots to resize it
Slice: cut the space with a plane, edit one side, then Restore view
Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Shift+Z (Ctrl+Y): undo / redo   ·   Ctrl+S: save (all point fields are kept)
Ctrl + right drag: take back with the brush (deselect, or clear labels) while the view stays still

Labelling mode (Ctrl+L):  B label brush   W smart pick
Ctrl+1 … Ctrl+9: label the selection with the n-th class   ·   Enter: active class   ·   Ctrl+0: clear the label
Alt + click: take the class under the cursor   ·   N: next unlabelled patch   ·   Ctrl+Alt+S: save labels only   ·   P: protect labelled points
Smart pick: click finds an object, a flat surface or a smooth surface; [ / ] loosen or tighten it
Frames folder:  , / . previous / next frame
Delete never removes points here: it clears the labels of the selection, or deletes the box / object clicked last in its list
Click the eye or lock in the class list header to switch it for every class
controls_grid:
Wheel or Ctrl+= / Ctrl+−: zoom   ·   Middle / right drag or Space + drag: pan   ·   Ctrl+0 / Home: fit

Tools:  H navigate   B pen   L line   R rectangle   G fill   I measure
O / F / U: paint occupied / free / unknown   ·   [ / ]: thinner / thicker pen
Shift (Line, Measure): lock to 0°, 45° or 90°
Shift (Rectangle): square   ·   Alt: draw from the centre
Shift + click (Pen): straight line from the last point

Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Shift+Z (Ctrl+Y): undo / redo   ·   Ctrl+S: save (YAML is written next to the image)
welcome_text:
A barbershop for robot maps.
Open or drop an OctoMap, a point cloud or a 2D occupancy grid — the right editor opens by itself.
brush_tip: Select/Erase use a cube with this edge length; Add places one layer of this width.
plane_tip: With the Add tool, clicking empty space places voxels on this horizontal plane.
islands_tip: Selects small groups of voxels that touch nothing else. Review them, then press Delete.
box_fill_tip: Marks every cell inside the box as occupied.
crop_tip: Keeps only the points inside the box.
range_tip: Anything outside this range is hidden and cannot be edited.
voxel_legend:
White: added since last save · Pink: selected
Axes at the map origin: x red, y green, z blue
cloud_legend:
Pink: selected
Axes at the cloud origin: x red, y green, z blue
grid_legend:
Black: occupied · White: free · Grey: unknown
Red and green arrows: map origin x and y
cloud_brush_tip: Select/Erase affect every point within this distance of the clicked point.
outliers_tip: Selects points whose average distance to their neighbours is far above the norm.
sparse_tip: Selects points with too few neighbours inside the search radius.
thin_tip: Keeps one point per cubic cell and removes the rest (undoable).
grid_brush_tip: Width of the pen and line tools in cells.
speckles_tip: Turns small isolated occupied blobs into free space.
trim_tip: Crops the unknown margin around the map and moves the origin so nothing shifts.
voxel_size_new: Voxel size of the new map [m]:
voxel_counts: Voxels {n} (visible {v})  ·  unsaved +{a} / −{r}  ·  selected {s}  ·  voxel size {res} m
status_islands: {n} islands, {m} voxels selected — review, then press Delete
status_filter: {n} points selected — review, then press Delete
status_converted: Converted the {source} to a {kind} — not saved yet
status_box_empty: The box contains no cell centre; enlarge it
empty_map: The map is empty; there is nothing to save.
box_too_large: The box holds {n} cells; the limit is 2,000,000.
box_handles_tip: Drag the coloured arrows in the 3D view to move the box along x, y or z, and the dots on its faces to resize it.
slice_tip: Cut the space with a plane and work on one side. The other side is hidden and protected until you restore the view.
status_view_restored: View restored — everything is visible again
ruler_tip: With the Measure tool, click two points to read the real distance between them.
ruler_tip_grid: With the Measure tool, click two cells to read the distance in metres and in pixels.
ruler_hint: Measure tool: click a first point, then a second.
ruler_second: First point set — click the second point
ruler_detail_voxel:
Distance {d:.3f} m  ·  {cells:.1f} voxels
Δx {dx:+.3f}   Δy {dy:+.3f}   Δz {dz:+.3f} m
ruler_detail_cloud:
Distance {d:.3f} m
Δx {dx:+.3f}   Δy {dy:+.3f}   Δz {dz:+.3f} m
ruler_detail_grid:
Distance {d:.3f} m  ·  {px:.1f} px
Δx {dx:+.3f} m   Δy {dy:+.3f} m
{dc:+d} × {dr:+d} cells
status_brush: {n} points in the brush  ·  {d:.2f} m from the camera
empty_as_free: Mark cells without an obstacle as free (otherwise unknown)
loss_intro: A {format} file cannot store everything this map holds. This will be left out:
loss_free_space: Free space: only occupied cells are written, the rest becomes unknown
loss_values: Occupancy values: every cell is written as simply occupied or free
loss_elements: Other parts of the PLY file: {detail}
class_remove_tip: Takes the class off the list; points keep their number and can be given a class again.
class_wins_tip: When points become voxels, a voxel holding even one point of this class takes this class. Use it for things a map must never miss, such as people or thin obstacles.
class_list_tip:
Click a class to make it active. Ctrl+1 … Ctrl+9 label the selection with the first nine classes, Ctrl+0 clears it.
👁 hides a class: hidden points cannot be selected, labelled or erased.
🔒 locks a class: its points keep their label.
role_tip: What this class means when the cloud becomes a voxel map or a 2D grid: obstacles are kept, free surface (floor, road) marks cells as free, ignored classes (people, noise) can be left out.
rule_tip: Which points the brush, the smart pick and Enter may write to: every point, only points without a label, or only points of one class (to correct one class without touching the others). Locked classes are never changed.
label_assign_tip: Map the selected points to the active class (Enter). Ctrl+1 … Ctrl+9 map them to the n-th class directly.
label_solo_tip: Show only the active class; press again to show everything.
labels_load_tip: Read labels from a file (SemanticKITTI .label, .npz, .npy or one number per line), for example a model's predictions. They arrive as suggestions to confirm.
labels_only_tip: Write the labels next to the cloud (name.labels.npz) and leave the cloud file itself untouched.
labels_only_refused: Points were erased, so the labels no longer match the file. Save the whole cloud instead.
labels_count: The file holds {n} labels but the cloud has {m} points.
smart_tip: Click a point with the Smart pick tool (W): it selects the object, flat patch or smooth surface around it. Enter labels the result; [ and ] loosen or tighten the last pick. Ctrl + click removes from the selection.
smart_too_many: {n} points within reach; make the search distance smaller.
status_smart: {n} points picked; Enter labels them, [ / ] adjust
review_next_tip: Select the largest unlabelled patch in view and move the camera to it (N).
review_disagree_tip: Labelled points that most of their neighbours contradict: brush slips and ragged borders.
review_islands_tip: Small detached patches of a class, often stray strokes.
review_fill_tip: Unlabelled points take the majority class of labelled points around them, as suggestions (shown pale) to confirm or reject.
review_done: Every visible point has a label.
instance_own_tip: Every label mapping / smart pick also starts a new object number, so separate objects of one class stay apart.
instance_split_tip: Every connected group of the selection (or, with nothing selected, of the active class) becomes its own object. Groups never span two classes or two frames; the gap comes from Smart pick.
boxes_tip: Upright 3D boxes (centre, size, yaw, class, object) for objects, saved with the labels: name.boxes.json beside a cloud, boxes/<frame>.json in a frames folder.
boxes_none: No objects on screen: split a class into objects first, or make a box from a selection.
frames_tip: Pick one frame, a range (Shift) or any few frames (Ctrl), then Show. The chosen frames are merged by their poses; labels stay with the frame each point came from.
frames_paint_tip: Restrict labelling to one frame, for example to mark a moving object in a single scan while others are overlaid.
frames_propagate_tip: Labels of classes not marked 'ignore' are carried from the frames on screen to every other frame, point by point within the match distance. They arrive as suggestions; moving objects are not carried.
frames_conflicts_tip: Points whose label differs from a point of another frame at the same place.
frames_need_poses: Carrying labels between frames needs poses (poses.txt next to the frames).
frames_no_erase: Frames are labelled, not edited: erasing is off. Open a single frame file to remove points.
recover_text: Labels of this file were not saved when MapBarber last closed. Bring them back?
voxel_labels_tip: Each voxel takes the class most of its points carry (classes marked 'wins' take a voxel with a single point). Relabel voxels here; turning the map back into points gives every point its own label again, except in voxels you relabelled.
purity_tip: Voxels whose points did not agree: the share of points carrying the voxel's class is below this value.
relabel_back: {n} voxels were relabelled here. Their points will take the new class; every other point keeps its own label. Continue?
loss_points: The link to the original points: per-point labels and fields stay only in this open tab
frames_many: {n} frames hold about {p} points, more than is comfortable to edit at once. Show them anyway?
loss_pending: Unconfirmed suggestions: {detail} suggested labels would be saved as ordinary labels (confirm or reject them in Review first)
welcome_voxel: OctoMap .bt / .ot and voxel archives: trim, fill and label voxels.
welcome_cloud: PCD, PLY, LAS/LAZ, KITTI .bin and text: clean and label points, one scan or many frames.
welcome_grid: ROS map_server YAML + PGM/PNG: paint, erase and fix 2D occupancy maps.
welcome_any_tip: Any supported file; its type is recognised automatically. You can also drop files or folders on the window.
label_mode_tip: Switch to labelling (Ctrl+L): label brush, smart pick, classes, review and instances. Switch off to return to editing exactly as it was.
label_mode_on: Labelling mode: B label brush, W smart pick, Ctrl+1 … 9 label the selection. Ctrl+L returns to editing.
label_protect_tip: Labelled points stay out of selections and keep their label, so a wide selection (a wall, the floor) skips the objects labelled before. P toggles it.
label_legend: Label colours: pale = suggested, not yet confirmed
class_removed: Class “{name}” removed — Ctrl+Z brings it back
timeline_tip: Drag a handle to set the first or last frame, or drag the blue band to slide the range. A click anywhere else on this strip, the frame numbers included, changes nothing and only takes the keyboard. Green ticks: frames with labels, amber: changed and not saved. Then ← / → slide the range by its own width (Shift + arrow: by one frame).
ground_tip: Finds the lowest surface under the visible points that nowhere rises steeper than the slope; points within the height above it are ground. Points far below it (noise) are not ground. Select it to erase it, to keep only what stands on it, or to label it (Enter).
frames_poses_none: none — frames are shown as they are
frames_poses_tip: A text file with one pose per frame or a timed trajectory: 3x4 or 4x4 matrices, [time] x y z qx qy qz qw (TUM), or columns named in a header (time, x, y, z, qx qy qz qw or roll pitch yaw). When the frame file names carry times, poses are matched and interpolated by time.
frames_no_poses_tip: For frames that already share one coordinate frame.
smart_clearance_tip: Connected points: points within this height of the ground join nothing, so whatever rests on the ground comes without it (0 = off). This is what separates objects from the ground in sparse LiDAR scans. The ground comes from the Ground filter's cell size and slope.
instance_min_tip: Groups with fewer points get no instance number (fragments, stray points).
instance_clear_tip: The selection (or, with nothing selected, the active class) keeps its class and drops its instance numbers: from instance segmentation back to semantic segmentation.
instance_list_tip: Click an object to select its points and look at it.
status_instances: {n} objects; {s} points in fragments too small to count
boxes_fit_tip: An upright box around every instance on screen (in a sequence: per frame, in the sensor frame). Boxes you made from a selection stay.
smart_stop_bends_tip: Connected points: where the surface direction changes by more than the bend angle over many points — a wide floor, wall or table top (wider than a third of the search range) — the search stops. Needs dense data: single sparse LiDAR scans give no reliable directions, so there the ground clearance does the work.
class_all_tip: Click the eye or the lock here to switch it for every class at once.
boxes_class_tip: The box workflow for the active class: its points are split into separate objects (those without an object number yet), and each object gets an upright 3D box. Run it again after relabelling to refresh the boxes of this class.
label_export_tip: Write the labels where other tools and training code expect them: a SemanticKITTI sequence (velodyne/*.bin, labels/*.label, poses, semantic-kitti.yaml), KITTI object labels (label_2/*.txt) and OpenPCDet boxes (x y z dx dy dz heading class).
instance_gap_tip: Points closer than this belong to the same object. Sparse LiDAR scans need more (0.5 m), dense scans less.
track: Track boxes through the frames on screen
track_reach_tip: How far an object may have moved between two frames beyond its own speed.
track_accept_tip: Score = half box overlap (IoU) + half point alignment (ICP fitness). At or above this the labels are applied; below it they arrive as suggestions marked '?' to review; below 0.25 the track ends.
track_tip: Box the objects in the first frame (Box every object of …), set the frame range on the timeline, then track: each object is found in the next frame by box overlap, its points are aligned to it (ICP), and its class, object number and box are carried along with a score.
track_none: Nothing to track: the first frame on screen needs boxed objects, and later frames must be on screen (widen the timeline range).
